lakitu: install EFI bootloaders into /boot/efi/boot An auto update payload doesn't include ESP (EFI System Partition, which is partition # 12). Hence, if we want the EFI bootloaders to be updated by auto update, we should put the EFI bootloaders in the root filesystem's /boot directory and should let the installer (src/platform2/installer/chromeos_legacy.cc, specifically) copy the EFI bootloaders from the root filesystem's /boot to ESP. The change for installer is CL:1003518. When building a full image, the build scripts (src/scripts/update_bootloaders.sh, specifically) copy these from root filesystem's /boot to ESP. BUG=b:69569602 TEST=The bootloader files are installed in /boot of the root filesystem, and they are copied to the ESP (EFI System Partition), which is /dev/sda12, as well. And they are launched by UEFI firmware. With legacy BIOS, the behavior hasn't changed (The old Grub boots like before). RELEASE_NOTE=None Change-Id: Ica2b6920003431750485604facad045170ebff7c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1003528 Commit-Ready: Edward Jee <edjee@google.com> Tested-by: Edward Jee <edjee@google.com> Reviewed-by: Edward Jee <edjee@google.com>

lakitu: remove legacy EFI bootloaders The legacy EFI bootloaders (bootx64.efi, bootia32.efi) are an old version of Grub. Neither legacy BIOS nor UEFI firmware uses them in lakitu image. As those legacy EFI bootloaders do not support secure boot or measured boot, it's better to remove them for security. The legacy EFI bootloaders are generated by src/scripts/build_library/create_legacy_bootloader_templates.sh. Because that script is a ChromiumOS-wide one, we choose to leave the script as is and remove the legacy EFI bootloaders afterward, only for lakitu. BUG=b:69569602 TEST=Normally boots, with both legacy BIOS and UEFI firmware. CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: scarlet: Don't use pinctrl controller hogs for BT and WiFi pins On Scarlet we use a hack involving pinctrl and GPIO driven (fake-) regulators to reset the Bluetooth and WiFi controllers at boot. The hack works like this: The BT_EN and WLAN_EN pins are configured as pinctrl controller hogs to drive them low early in the boot process. Further we have GPIO enabled fake-regulators that drive the corresponding pin to high when the controller is enabled. This scheme worked fine, until commit 3f0ad8ee1d4a ("pinctrl: Really force states during suspend/resume") changed the behavior of pinctrl controller hogs at resume. The change consists in reapplying the default pin configuration at resume, which ends up driving BT/WLAN_EN pins to low. Disabled Bluetooth and WiFi on its own would be annoying enough, but since the system is not aware that the controllers are disabled it keeps accessing them, which leads to system crashes on resume as reported in b/77863555. Instead of using controller hogs the pins could be tied to the fake- regulator devices involved in the hack, which would avoid the problem. However it turns out that pinctrl is not needed (directly) to drive the pins low. When the regulators are registered they are disabled, in consequence regulator_register() sets the pin to low when it requests the GPIO. With the pinctrl controller hogs the BT/WLAN_EN was deasserted for +150ms, when relying on regulator_register() (or pinctrl settings tied to the regulator) this time is reduced to about 60ms, which is still more than enough to reset the controllers: [ 0.128412] DBG: setting GPIO 0.8 to 0 [ 0.128639] DBG: set mux of pin 0.8 to 0 [ 0.129072] DBG: set mux of pin 0.5 to 0 [ 0.129252] rockchip-pinctrl pinctrl: DBG: setting pull of GPIO0-5 to 5 [ 0.129479] DBG: setting GPIO 0.4 to 0 [ 0.129673] DBG: set mux of pin 0.4 to 0 [ 0.192842] DBG: setting GPIO 0.8 to 1 [ 0.193086] DBG: setting GPIO 0.4 to 1 BUG=b:77863555 TEST=suspend dru and resume Change-Id: I45e8abd7a4e4d060aa13d10fc2a9fd009755a1fe Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1009023 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ath10k: fix use-after-free in ath10k_wmi_cmd_send_nowait The skb may be freed in tx completion context before trace_ath10k_wmi_cmd is called. This can be easily captured when KASAN(Kernel Address Sanitizer) is enabled. The fix is to move trace_ath10k_wmi_cmd before the send operation. As the ret has no meaning in trace_ath10k_wmi_cmd then, so remove this parameter too. [autotest] Don't detect labels with `deploy servo`. The intent of `deploy servo` is that it not require a working DUT. However, as constructed, `deploy servo` still attempts to do automatic label detection, which _does_ require a working DUT. So, don't run the label detection during the `deploy servo` command. [autotest] Update lab_inventory to report idle DUTs with metrics. This updates the lab_inventory script to report DUTs that are idle and unlocked via a new Monarch metric.
